title: In WWII, a Famous Psychologist Trained Pigeons to Steer Missiles

scenes.text: In World War Two, the US trained pigeons to steer missiles.
Psychologist B. F. Skinner put three pigeons in a missile's nose.
They watched a screen and pecked at the target.
Their pecks moved cables that steered the missile.
The pigeons worked. Years later, they still passed his tests.
The military never trusted it, and cancelled the program.

description:
In 1943 psychologist B. F. Skinner began Project Pigeon, a plan to use trained pigeons to guide missiles.
Three birds sat in the nose cone, saw the target on screens and pecked to steer. The demo worked, but officials stayed sceptical and ended the project. A prototype is in the Smithsonian.
Would you have trusted a pigeon pilot? Comment below.
first_comment: Skinner tested the same pigeons one, two, four and six years later and they still performed. Would you trust your life to a pigeon?
